events.title: Barrel Age Your Own Sake — A Brooklyn Kura Workshop Class
events.description:
Skill Level : Beginner-friendly, no coopering or sake knowledge required.
What You’ll Be Making : A handmade oak barrel, suitable for aging your own sake or shochu. The barrel will hold approximately 2 liters of liquid.
What You’ll Be Doing: You’ll assemble, shape, char, and personalize your barrel before filling it with a sake or shochu hand-picked by Brooklyn Kura for aging.
What’s Included? All barrel-making materials and tools, guided sake and shochu tasting flight, take your barrel home the same day
What To Expect
Right next door in Industry City, a small team is brewing junmai sake with some of the cleanest tap water in the country. Spend an afternoon with them and you’ll leave with two things: a handmade oak barrel built stave by stave with your own hands, and a palate for sake you didn’t have when you walked in. Char the inside with a torch, seat the heads, brand it with your initials — then fill it with something Brooklyn Kura hand-picked just for aging.
What You’ll Create
A functional 2-liter oak barrel, coopered from scratch — same craft, same tools, same afternoon of assembling staves and hoops, cutting crozes on the router table, and charring the interior until it’s ready for spirits. This time, what goes in it isn’t whiskey. It’s rice, koji, yeast, and water, aged into something you helped choose.
The Tasting Flight
A sake expert from Brooklyn Kura walks you through a flight of three sakes and a shochu, all brewed or distilled right here in Industry City, all selected because they take well to a little time in wood. The lineup changes with the seasons, but here’s what’s been on the table:
**Grand Prairie — a Junmai Ginjo built around white peach, jasmine, and toasted rice.
**Occidental — a dry-hopped Junmai, bringing out lychee, grapefruit, and cherry that age into deeper dried-fruit notes. Tidal — a fuller-bodied
**Junmai, all steamed rice, apple, and cereal bran.
**Kura Shochu — distilled from the leftover sake lees, rich with fig and custard and a rice umami built for barrel aging.
What Sake and Shochu Actually Are
Brooklyn Kura brews junmai-style sake — no additives, just four ingredients doing all the work. Rice sets the structure; the strain and how far it’s polished shape the flavor before brewing even starts. Koji, the fungus that turns starch to sugar, decides how sweet and umami-forward or light and aromatic the sake ends up. Yeast supplies the fruit, flower, and herb notes, which is why a batch often blends more than one strain. And water — helped along by some of the purest tap water in the country — is what makes the whole thing clean and crisp instead of muddy.
Shochu takes a different road. Where sake is brewed like wine or beer, shochu is distilled like whiskey or vodka. Kura starts with kasu, the leftover lees from sake-making, re-ferments it with a shochu-specific koji, and distills it into something rich and complex — closer to a young rice whiskey than anything else, and exactly the kind of spirit that rewards time in a barrel.
Finishing the Night at Kura
Your barrel’s made, your glass is empty — Brooklyn Kura is a short walk across Industry City, and your Craftsman Ave ticket gets you a discount on sake or shochu to take home and age. They’ve got a full kitchen too: mac and cheese, little smoky sausages, house-made focaccia. Good reason to stay a while longer.

events.title: Body Talk
events.description:
This event is free to the public but a sliding scale suggested donation of $10–$15. No one will be turned away for lack of funds — everyone is welcome to participate regardless of ability to pay.
RSVP is required here.
About the event:
Body Talks are workshops that employ Imani’s poetic approach to somatic healing grounded in creativity, mindfulness, movement, and more. Body Talks invite us into deeper intimacy with ourselves and other Body Talkers, grounding us in collective somatic healing intended to liberate us.
These workshops invite queer and trans adults into spaces of deep intimacy that ground our liberation work in collective somatic healing.
Signature Body Talks support participants to:
Begin an intuitive dialogue between body and mind and their relationship with creativity and space.
Cultivate healing collaboration between the left-side brain (speech, abstract thinking) and right-side brain (image processing, spatial thinking).
Engage the spiritual and somatic aspects of healing trauma simultaneously
Practice slow, progressive somatic engagement with the nervous system (titration) through several artistic mediums
Reconnect with embodied, ancestral knowledge and wisdom.
Body Talks are educational spaces. We share ourselves, our creativity, and embodied wisdom as resources for collective mental and somatic liberation.

SLOT 4: 5:30 pm - 6:00 pm Register Here
About: On Mondays from 4:00pm-6:00pm the Brooklyn Community Pride Center in partnership with Rachel Goldstein (she/her/hers), a Licensed Clinical Social Worker, will be offering free letters of support and counseling for community members seeking gender-affirming surgeries and procedures.
These free appointments are by appointment only. This service is available to adults ages 18 and older only.
Time: Each appointment will be 30 minutes
Location: Appointments can be scheduled virtually via Zoom, or take place in person at the Brooklyn Community Pride Center. During the registration process you can select which location option you prefer. If you select virtual, and the appointment is approved, you will be sent the Zoom meeting details.
About Rachel Goldstein: I am really excited to be offering some walk-in counseling hours and free evaluations for letters of support if you are getting gender affirming surgery. I am dedicated to creating a safe, non- judgmental and comfortable holding space for you to feel supported, wherever you are and in whatever you are going through. My goal is that you leave my office knowing you have been heard, seen and affirmed regardless of gender, race, sexual orientation, age, immigration status or education level. I am constantly in awe of our shared humanity, resiliency and ability to adapt.
A little about me…I received my graduate degrees in both Social Work and Special Education in 2000. I work using strengths based, trauma informed care and have expertise in reproductive healthcare, LGBTQ+ care, addictions, sexual violence, Ketamine Assisted Psychotherapy, crisis intervention, self-injury and trans health. The past 9 years of my career have been focused on working alongside medical providers who provide Gender Affirming Hormone Therapy at Planned Parenthood of Greater NY (where I have been a SW for 16 years). I am committed to bodily autonomy, lifelong learning, reproductive justice, advocacy and cultural humility.  Every day I learn from my patients whom I trust deeply as the experts in their own experiences.

events.title: Unchained Friendsgiving Dinner
events.description:
Join us for Friendsgiving, a special gathering for the LGBT+ Caribbean community to reconnect, heal, and celebrate our shared journeys. Enjoy free Caribbean catering, build meaningful connections, and honor our resilience this holiday season. RSVP now and be part of this heartwarming celebration filled with gratitude, and togetherness! https://bit.ly/UnchainedFriendsgiving
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Launched in 2015, Unchained is a pioneering initiative in New York City, offering a culturally responsive, unique peer-to-peer support group through the Caribbean Equality Project. For a decade, Unchained has been at the heart of our Healing Justice work, providing an empowering space for Caribbean LGBT+ immigrants, those impacted by HIV, and survivors of family rejection, discrimination, intimate partner violence, and sexual assault to heal and build community.
Unchained is dedicated to creating a compassionate environment where individuals can embrace their cultural identities and experiences as Queeribbeans. Our goal is to provide hyper-local healing spaces in neighborhoods with strong Caribbean ties, such as Little Caribbean in Brooklyn and Little Guyana in Queens.
Our members find solace and support in conversations and creative healing around coming out, family dynamics, LGBTQIA+ issues, social norms, healthy relationships and dating, sexual fluidity, and overall health and wellness. We’re excited to offer a warm, welcoming space for Caribbean LGBT+ immigrants, those living with HIV, and survivors of family rejection, discrimination, intimate partner violence, and sexual assault to heal and build community. Here, you’ll find guidance and understanding as we navigate a collective journey of storytelling and reflection, rich in culture and intention. We can’t wait to welcome you to Unchained!
L (they/them), Healing Justice Coordinator organizes and facilitates both Queens and Brooklyn Unchained.
Registration is REQUIRED. Dinner, MetroCards, and Incentives are provided and informed by RSVP’s. Sign up here

events.description:
All players must register through Meetup so we can ensure that we have enough games planned!
We welcome everyone interested in role playing games, whether you’ve never picked up a set of dice before or you’ve been running games for 20 years. We work hard to intentionally create a fun, supportive, and inclusive environment to explore new games and old favorites. Bring your co-workers, friends, and partners, too!We understand that it’s hard to commit to an ongoing RPG. That’s why each of our games concludes in a single session and requires no player prep or ongoing commitment. If you are looking for longer-term games, this is a great group to connect with other players and GMs who are looking for the same.Each session, we bring several different tabletop RPGs to the table, and the options are different every Meetup! Most of them are indie and small publisher games, though occasionally you might see a game of D&D if there is demand. We've played over 50 different RPGs across more than 30 Meetups and can likely organize a table to run that obscure game you've always wanted to try! If you’re a game designer looking for playtesters, you’ll find a willing table with us. Here are some of the games we could potentially run: http://bit.ly/nycttrpgs
Please gather at 5:30 PM to check in. Game selection will begin promptly at 6:00 PM. If you arrive significantly later than that, we will most likely be able to find a game you can join, but there is a small chance there won’t be any open spaces left.

Guidance:

Together, we’ll move through accessible posture sequences, grounding breathwork, and deep rest in an environment where every expression of identity, body type, and ability level is fully honored. Body Talks are workshops that employ Imani’s poetic approach to somatic healing grounded in creativity, mindfulness, movement, and more. Body Talks invite us into deeper intimacy with ourselves and other Body Talkers, grounding us in collective somatic healing intended to liberate us.
These workshops invite queer and trans adults into spaces of deep intimacy that ground our liberation work in collective somatic healing.
Signature Body Talks support participants to:
Begin an intuitive dialogue between body and mind and their relationship with creativity and space.
Cultivate healing collaboration between the left-side brain (speech, abstract thinking) and right-side brain (image processing, spatial thinking).
Engage the spiritual and somatic aspects of healing trauma simultaneously
Practice slow, progressive somatic engagement with the nervous system (titration) through several artistic mediums
Reconnect with embodied, ancestral knowledge and wisdom.
Body Talks are educational spaces. We share ourselves, our creativity, and embodied wisdom as resources for collective mental and somatic liberation.

events.description:
Join us for the Annual Unchained Holiday Talent Showcase on December 21st to celebrate creativity, joy, and community through music, dance, and laughter. With free Caribbean catering and a welcoming space for all, let’s honor our uniqueness and remind ourselves that we belong this holiday season. https://bit.ly/UnchainedTalent
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Launched in 2015, Unchained is a pioneering initiative in New York City, offering a culturally responsive, unique peer-to-peer support group through the Caribbean Equality Project. For a decade, Unchained has been at the heart of our Healing Justice work, providing an empowering space for Caribbean LGBT+ immigrants, those impacted by HIV, and survivors of family rejection, discrimination, intimate partner violence, and sexual assault to heal and build community.
Unchained is dedicated to creating a compassionate environment where individuals can embrace their cultural identities and experiences as Queeribbeans. Our goal is to provide hyper-local healing spaces in neighborhoods with strong Caribbean ties, such as Little Caribbean in Brooklyn and Little Guyana in Queens.
Our members find solace and support in conversations and creative healing around coming out, family dynamics, LGBTQIA+ issues, social norms, healthy relationships and dating, sexual fluidity, and overall health and wellness. We’re excited to offer a warm, welcoming space for Caribbean LGBT+ immigrants, those living with HIV, and survivors of family rejection, discrimination, intimate partner violence, and sexual assault to heal and build community. Here, you’ll find guidance and understanding as we navigate a collective journey of storytelling and reflection, rich in culture and intention. We can’t wait to welcome you to Unchained!
L (they/them), Healing Justice Coordinator organizes and facilitates both Queens and Brooklyn Unchained.

events.title: Tabletop Role Playing Games
events.description:
All players must register through Meetup so we can ensure that we have enough games planned!
We welcome everyone interested in role playing games, whether you’ve never picked up a set of dice before or you’ve been running games for 20 years. We work hard to intentionally create a fun, supportive, and inclusive environment to explore new games and old favorites. Bring your co-workers, friends, and partners, too!We understand that it’s hard to commit to an ongoing RPG. That’s why each of our games concludes in a single session and requires no player prep or ongoing commitment. If you are looking for longer-term games, this is a great group to connect with other players and GMs who are looking for the same.Each session, we bring several different tabletop RPGs to the table, and the options are different every Meetup! Most of them are indie and small publisher games, though occasionally you might see a game of D&D if there is demand. We've played over 50 different RPGs across more than 30 Meetups and can likely organize a table to run that obscure game you've always wanted to try! If you’re a game designer looking for playtesters, you’ll find a willing table with us. Here are some of the games we could potentially run: http://bit.ly/nycttrpgs
Please gather at 5:30 PM to check in. Game selection will begin promptly at 6:00 PM. If you arrive significantly later than that, we will most likely be able to find a game you can join, but there is a small chance there won’t be any open spaces left.
